answer: A stake-bonded reputation registry resists sybils: each agent locks a refundable deposit to register one identity, returned only after a long honest history. A fake army must fund every copy, so cost grows linearly while one honest agent pays once. Good reputation spreads like a ripple from verified work, and bad behavior slashes the bond. At the zenith of trust, a real history is worth more than fresh clones, because a spiral of attestations from genuine counterparties cannot be forged cheaply.
